question: Could an authentic public individual initially localized EMC cohort determine whether a first distant event commonly occurs without a preceding local recurrence, with exact event ordering and observation/competing-death histories, beyond authors already published aggregate recurrence prognosis?
patient_care_value_gate: Only a materially unreported reliable conditional event pathway could justify testing whether local-only follow-up misses distant-first disease; no surveillance schedule or treatment recommendation follows from a small retrospective cohort. Re-expressing known persistent late metastasis or published local/distant proportions is insufficient.
scope: All eligible initially localized native-EMC patients and unfavorable/ambiguous conditions in every advancing source; baseline metastatic cases kept separate. Histologic author diagnoses and molecular confirmation are distinct.
required_data: An explicit case-key crosswalk with event dates or durations tied to one common time origin, correct censorship, complete local/distant/death ascertainment; no ever-event/final-followup substitution, no Kaplan-Meier digitization/reconstruction.
strongest_alternatives: prior art already reports the same order or absence of local prerequisite
referral/delayed-entry and detection schedule determine apparent sequence

published source already answers useful contrast
tiny descriptive or selected case inventory cannot refine useful measurement
accessible relevant pending mappings block promotion
